🚀 plainpad | PHP
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide a private and secure self-hosted solution for individuals and teams to manage their notes.
✨ Key Features: • Self-hosted note taking • Data ownership • Simplicity and stability • Docker setup
📖 Summary: Plainpad is a self-hosted note-taking application built with PHP and React, offering users full ownership of their data. It emphasizes simplicity and stability, running on the user's own server.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ rip | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: Interactively finding and terminating unwanted or problematic processes from the terminal using a fuzzy search interface.
✨ Key Features: • Fuzzy process finding • Interactive terminal interface • Process killing with customizable signals • Sorting by CPU, memory, PID, name, and port • Live mode with auto-refreshing process list
📖 Summary: Rip is a command-line tool written in Rust that allows users to fuzzy find and terminate processes running on their system. It provides an interactive interface to search for processes by name, sort them by various metrics like CPU, memory, or PID, and send signals (like KILL or TERM) to selected processes.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 time-tracker-4-browser | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Helping users understand, manage, and improve their browsing habits by tracking time spent on websites, setting limits, and blocking distracting sites.
✨ Key Features: • Track browsing time and visit counts • Detailed records and daily activity review • Dashboards, website analysis, and habit reports
📖 Summary: Time Tracker - Web Habit Builder is a browser extension designed to help users understand and manage their online habits. It provides detailed tracking of website usage, analytical reports, website blocking, and focus tools like Pomodoro sessions, with cross-browser compatibility and data synchronization/backup options.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 mana | HTML
🎯 Primary Use Case: Conducting rogue access point attacks and Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks.
✨ Key Features: • Modified hostapd for KARMA attacks (hostapd-mana) • Controller scripts for managing attacks (run-mana) • Tools for offloading EAP credential cracking (crackapd) • Modifications for sslstrip and HSTS bypass • Apache configurations for specific hacks
📖 Summary: The MANA Toolkit is a deprecated collection of tools designed for rogue access point (evilAP) attacks and Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) scenarios. It includes modified hostapd for enhanced KARMA attacks and utilities for post-connection MitM operations.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ osx-and-ios-security-awesome | Shell
🎯 Primary Use Case: To serve as a centralized, curated resource for security professionals, researchers, and enthusiasts looking for tools to analyze, audit, and secure macOS and iOS systems.
✨ Key Features: • Curated list of macOS security tools • Curated list of iOS security tools • Categorization of tools by function (forensics, auditing, persistence, etc.) • Links to external repositories and projects • Includes tools for binary whitelisting, code injection, and disassembling
📖 Summary: This repository is an 'Awesome List' curating a comprehensive collection of security-related tools specifically for macOS and iOS. It categorizes these tools for forensic analysis, system auditing, malware detection, and security configuration management.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 Interlace | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: To accelerate and scale the execution of single-threaded command-line tools, particularly in security and network enumeration tasks, by allowing them to run concurrently against a large number of targets defined using CIDR or glob patterns.
✨ Key Features: • Multi-threading for command-line applications • CIDR notation support for targets • Glob support for targets • Exclusion lists for targets • Customizable thread count and timeouts
📖 Summary: Interlace is a Python-based tool designed to enhance single-threaded command-line applications by enabling multi-threading. It simplifies the process of running these applications concurrently against multiple targets, supporting CIDR notation for IP ranges and glob patterns for file matching.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source
